newsitem.title: USA: Disney foreign box office tops $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: Disney foreign box office tops $1 billion.

text.p: Buena Vista International, Walt Disney Co.'s worldwide film distribution wing, said Thursday its films topped $1.0 billion in foreign box office sales for the second straight year.
International ticket sales amounted to $1.007 billion in 1995 and $963 million in 1994, Buena Vista said in a statement. Three movies -- "The Hunchback of Notre Dame", "Toy Story"
and the thriller "The Rock" -- combined for nearly half the total. "The Rock" has generated $194.5 million internationally, while "Toy Story" has taken in $159.2 million and "Hunchback" $140 million.

But "Hunchback", currently a top box office performer in Europe, is well on its way to scoring over $200 million in total sales in the international arena, the company said. It has been No. 1 in France and Germany for three weeks.

"We owe this year's success to a combination of a sensational mix of product, both animated and live-action, coupled with marketing and distribution expertise," said Mark Zoradi, president of the Disney unit.
The year ahead will be highlighted by overseas releases of "Ransom," the kidnap drama starring Mel Gibson, and the live-action version of the classic cartoon "101 Dalmations".
In the United States, "Ransom" has sold $117.5 million worth of tickets in five weeks on the market. "101 Dalmations" has sold $75.5 million in two weeks, according to industry trade publications.
